stories.title: Ukraine's wartime economy shows strain in Kyiv's shuttered restaurants
body: Reuters reported on 22 November that empty storefronts and closing restaurants are increasingly visible along Kyiv's Khreshchatyk. This illustrates civilian economic pressure but is not itself a national estimate of business closures.

stories.title: China asks Switzerland to help defuse European trade tensions
body: On 23 November, China's foreign minister Wang Yi urged his Swiss counterpart to support a resolution of China–EU trade disagreements and oppose Taiwanese independence. The comments are a Chinese diplomatic position, not a Swiss policy commitment or a concluded trade agreement.

stories.title: Labour outlines a larger public role in water and energy utilities
body: On 23 November, Reuters reported that senior minister Louise Haigh would set out the Labour government's case for greater public control of utilities at the CBI conference. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has criticised weak regulation, high prices and sewage discharges. The government describes its approach as a partnership with private investors, not a completed programme of nationalisation. A planned speech is not enacted policy.

stories.title: Cross-party MPs press for public ownership registers in overseas territories
body: A group of British MPs urged Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to compel overseas territories to disclose company beneficial owners. Parliament legislated for transparency in 2018, but implementation has lagged. The British Virgin Islands argues its legitimate-interest access regime is proportionate; critics say restricted access undermines sanctions and anti-corruption scrutiny. The request is political pressure, not a new order.

stories.title: UK business activity slows slightly despite AI investment
body: The preliminary S&P Global composite purchasing managers' index slipped to 52.3 in November from 52.9 in October, Reuters reported on 23 November. Readings above 50 indicate expansion. Survey economist Chris Williamson interpreted the results as consistent with fourth-quarter growth of about 0.6%, but that is a survey-based estimate, not an official GDP result. Respondents reported weaker export services demand and property-market activity alongside AI-related investment.

stories.title: Democrats clinch incoming House majority, but new Congress has not convened
body: Associated Press reported on 23 November that Democrats had secured at least 258 House seats in the 2026 midterms, with four races unresolved. That would be the party's largest House majority since 1992; the new Congress begins in January 2027, so election results must not be confused with present legislative control. Democrats have outlined affordability and oversight priorities, while Republican leader Jim Jordan vowed opposition.

stories.title: Senate Republicans block Iran war-powers measure despite election losses
body: On 19 November, the Senate voted 51–48 against a resolution requiring President Donald Trump to end the Iran war or seek congressional approval. Three Republicans joined Democrats in support, while Democrat John Fetterman voted against. The House had previously approved the measure. The vote illustrates the gap between the incoming Democratic majority and the current Congress's power to constrain the administration.

stories.title: Democrats propose 2028 debate rule targeting secret political money
body: On 23 November, Democratic National Committee chair Ken Martin announced plans to require presidential hopefuls to disavow supporting super PACs and dark-money groups to qualify for party debates. The DNC is planning 12 debates across 2027 and 2028. The rule is a party-controlled participation condition, not a nationwide campaign-finance ban; its practical enforceability remains uncertain.

stories.title: India announces $1.62 billion Nepal flood-recovery package
body: Following talks on 23 November in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an assistance package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees, approximately $1.62 billion, for reconstruction after Nepal's devastating August floods. Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit also saw the inauguration of cross-border infrastructure projects. An announced package is a commitment, not proof that every rupee has already been disbursed; reconstruction needs have been estimated at several billion dollars.

stories.title: Bangladesh warns Hasina will be arrested if she returns
body: In a Reuters interview published on 23 November, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs said former prime minister Sheikh Hasina would be arrested if she returns from India in December. Dhaka is seeking extradition; India had not publicly answered the latest appeal. The announcement follows bombings, arson and protests involving rival political factions. Claims about responsibility for violence are disputed by the government and Hasina's Awami League.

stories.title: Bangladesh's unrest also exposes garment workers' wage grievances
body: Reuters reporting from 19 November described garment workers blocking roads to demand higher wages while protests over Sheikh Hasina's proposed return disrupted transport and commerce. The labour actions were separate from the political mobilisation and should not be conflated with it. Bangladesh's export-dependent clothing industry makes prolonged disruption consequential for both workers and manufacturers.

stories.title: Supreme Court's scheduled docket includes electoral-roll challenges
body: The Indian Express reported that the Supreme Court's 23 November cause list included petitions about the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in West Bengal, alongside Delhi air pollution and other rights-related cases. A listing does not mean a final judgment has been issued.

stories.title: Samajwadi Party and Congress plan seat-sharing talks
body: The Indian Express reported that Uttar Pradesh's Samajwadi Party and Congress were due to hold seat-sharing discussions on 23 November, with Ram Gopal Yadav representing the SP leadership. Talks are not an agreement on constituencies.

stories.title: India–Nepal recovery agreement expands New Delhi's regional commitments
body: India's $1.62 billion package announced on 23 November follows August floods that killed around 1,500 people in Nepal. New Delhi's response has regional significance because Nepal depends on Indian fuel supplies and increasingly exports hydropower to India. The funding is a bilateral commitment; delivery, project allocation and reconstruction outcomes require later scrutiny.

stories.title: Bombay High Court eases Naresh Goyal's medical travel conditions
body: The Bombay High Court relaxed bail conditions for Jet Airways founder Naresh Goyal, allowing overseas medical treatment without requiring fresh trial-court permission for every trip, according to The Indian Express. This is a bail-condition decision, not a disposition of the underlying case.

stories.title: Mumbai records mixed air quality and below-normal morning temperatures
body: The Indian Express reported a 23 November city AQI of 152, while Colaba and Malad registered 266 and 206 respectively. IMD minimum temperatures were 20.1°C at Santacruz and 22.2°C at Colaba, each modestly below local normals. A single day's readings do not establish a climate trend.

stories.title: Thanksgiving streaming slate spans new dramas, comedies and franchise television
body: The Associated Press previewed releases scheduled for the week of 23–29 November, including Netflix's World War II film The Mosquito Bowl, Peacock comedy Dig with Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie, and Prime Video's Blade Runner 2099. These are release plans and editorial previews, not audience ratings or evidence that all titles are already available.

stories.title: Jennifer Lopez concert special and Peter Gabriel record headline music releases
body: The Associated Press reported that The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas was scheduled for CBS and Paramount+ on 26 November, while Peter Gabriel's 13-track companion album to i/o was due on 27 November. Scheduled release dates should not be presented as completed launches or commercial successes.

stories.title: Shabana Azmi challenges a comparison between India and Afghanistan over clothing
body: In comments reported by The Indian Express on 23 November, actor Shabana Azmi contrasted India's constitutional secular democracy with Afghanistan's theocratic government during a dispute over women's clothing choices. The remarks are part of a public political-cultural argument, not a change in law.

stories.title: India–New Zealand Wellington Test finishes drawn
body: New Zealand batted through the final day in Wellington on 23 November to secure a draw in the first Test against India, according to match reporting. The result is final, rather than a match preview.

stories.title: Pakistan A beat India A despite Tilak Varma century
body: The Indian Express reported that Tilak Varma scored 100 but Pakistan A won their Rising Stars Asia Cup meeting. The individual century did not translate into a team victory.

stories.title: AI investment doubts deepen the global equities retreat
body: Reuters reported on 23 November that Asian equities followed Wall Street lower after a sharp US selloff, as investors questioned the returns on large AI infrastructure spending. Market movements and assessments of future returns should be kept separate.

stories.title: Oil falls as traders weigh Iran-war supply risk
body: At 08:44 GMT on 23 November Reuters recorded Brent at $91.97 a barrel, down 0.65%, and US WTI at $82.92, down 0.59%. Attacks around Gulf shipping sustained a risk premium, while OPEC+ ministers were due to discuss 2027 policy on 29 November.

stories.title: Gold rebounds as the dollar's rally pauses
body: Reuters reported a rise of more than 2% in gold on 23 November as the US dollar's advance paused. The intraday move is not a final closing price or proof of a lasting reversal.

stories.title: Europe's inflation dilemma sharpens as ECB officials discuss another hike
body: On 23 November, ECB governing council member Gediminas Šimkus said a December rate increase might not fully contain inflation but another move need not follow immediately. Reuters reported that high energy costs had pushed inflation above the bank's 2% target. One policymaker's view is not an announced Governing Council decision.

stories.title: German private-sector PMI reaches its strongest level since early 2022
body: Reuters reported on 23 November that Germany's preliminary composite PMI rose to 55.0 from 53.4 in October, driven by manufacturing and services. The diffusion index points to faster expansion among survey respondents; it is not a measured percentage GDP growth rate.

stories.title: Indian equities retreat as financial shares weigh
body: Reuters reported on 23 November that financial stocks dragged Indian shares lower as investors took profits following four weeks of gains. The daily decline should be read against the preceding rally rather than as a stand-alone trend.

stories.title: November business survey finds factories offset weaker services growth
body: A November purchasing managers' survey cited by Reuters indicated a slight acceleration in private-sector activity, led by manufacturing demand and output, while services expansion moderated. PMI is a survey diffusion indicator, not an official GDP release.

stories.title: HDFC Bank treasury chief outlines a possible rupee recovery
body: HDFC Bank's treasury head told Reuters the rupee could strengthen to 91.50 per dollar if equity inflows support the currency. This is a conditional market forecast, not an observed exchange rate or RBI target.

stories.title: NASA-backed observations reveal an unusual stellar merger in Andromeda
body: NASA reported on 18 November that astronomers had identified a lower-mass star spiralling into and merging with a supergiant in the Andromeda galaxy. The team nicknamed the resulting object Bao and compared James Webb Space Telescope observations with other ground- and space-based measurements. The observations support a merger interpretation, while details of the star's later evolution remain a research question.

stories.title: New Arctic laser-ranging station strengthens satellite-orbit measurements
body: NASA Earth Observatory reported on 23 November that its next-generation satellite laser-ranging system began operating at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, on 12 October. The instrument times reflected laser pulses to refine satellite positions and the terrestrial reference frame, supporting sea-level, ice-mass and geodesy measurements. It is an instrumentation milestone, not a new measurement of climate change.

stories.title: US restrictions on advanced AI chips reshape Chinese technology strategy
body: Reuters reported on 20 November that tighter US restrictions on Chinese access to advanced AI computing, including remote data-centre capacity, were affecting Chinese technology shares and cloud expansion plans. Tencent said inference workloads could rely more on domestic chips, while Alibaba warned the curbs could constrain future services. These are company assessments and policy effects, not proof that domestic manufacturing can immediately replace leading-edge foreign supply.

stories.title: Cloud-sovereignty debate exposes Europe's dependence on US providers
body: A Reuters roundup on 23 November highlighted Europe's growing cloud-sovereignty initiatives alongside the continued dominance of US hyperscalers. Political aspirations for technological autonomy are not equivalent to immediate changes in market share.

stories.title: COP31 ends without a consensus political agreement
body: Reuters reported that the Antalya climate summit closed after the EU and other delegations rejected a draft that did not adequately address fossil-fuel transition. The failure of the overarching decision does not mean every technical negotiation produced no outcome. Turkey's presidency denied claims of preferential access for Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Saudi influence and carbon-capture language come under scrutiny
body: Reuters reported negotiators' allegations that Saudi Arabia had unusually strong access during COP31 and opposed explicit fossil-fuel transition language while promoting carbon capture. The presidency disputed preferential-treatment claims. Carbon capture language is not evidence of delivered or independently verified carbon removal.

stories.title: Pacific states and European negotiators explain COP31's breakdown
body: Delegates at COP31 in Antalya failed to agree on an overarching decision on 22 November. The Marshall Islands and European Union objected to language they considered too weak on fossil fuels, while Palau argued that even an imperfect draft could have advanced ocean, finance and electrification work. Their differing assessments demonstrate why the collapse of a political cover decision should not be equated with a total absence of technical progress.
